name: United States

income_tax.summary: US federal income tax only: 10% to 37% (2026 single brackets; standard deduction USD 16,100, modelled as the personal allowance). Austin, Texas adds no personal income tax: Texas has no state income tax and no local income tax was found for Austin. About 22% federal marginal rate at the 150,000 level. Employees pay 6.2% social security up to USD 184,500 plus 1.45% Medicare (plus 0.9% Additional Medicare Tax on wages above USD 200,000, not modelled); the self-employed pay 15.3% (12.4% + 2.9%) on 92.35% of net earnings. Other states vary widely: nine have no wage income tax (for example Texas and Florida).
income_tax.self_employed_notes: Self-employment tax is 15.3% (12.4% social security + 2.9% Medicare) applied to 92.35% of net self-employment earnings (IRS Schedule SE line 4a/5b, opened 2026-10-15), so the rate on net earnings is 15.3% x 0.9235 = 14.13%. The 12.4% part stops at the wage base (USD 184,500 for 2026, i.e. net earnings of about USD 199,783 after the 92.35% factor); the cap field uses that point, but the 2.9% Medicare part is uncapped and a 0.9% Additional Medicare Tax applies above USD 200,000 (single; IRS), neither modelled above the cap. Half of the SE tax is deductible in computing income tax (IRS), not modelled. Self-employed people may deduct the employer-equivalent half of self-employment tax (IRS, in adjusted gross income), so about 0.5 of their contributions reduce taxable income; the employee figure (0) governs the field.
income_tax.local_tax_note: Brackets are the 2026 US federal schedule for a single filer on TAXABLE income (IRS release), applied after the USD 16,100 standard deduction (field personal_allowance). Texas levies no state income tax (Texas Comptroller) and no Austin local income tax was found; the previous New York State and New York City layers were removed. Not modelled: the 0.9% Additional Medicare Tax on wages above USD 200,000 (employer withholding, single filer), the Net Investment Income Tax, itemised deductions, the QBI deduction, and FICA non-deductibility (social_security_deductible 0). Texas property tax and sales tax are not income taxes and are outside this field.

open_questions: Federal 2026 brackets and the USD 16,100 standard deduction are from the IRS release (the page is marked historical content); rates 10-37% follow the statutory schedule shown there.
Texas has no state income tax (Texas Comptroller); the absence of any Austin/Travis County local income tax was not separately sourced.
PwC's US pages give 2025 figures (self-employment wage base USD 176,100); the 2026 social security wage base (USD 184,500) is from the Journal of Accountancy.
The 0.9% Additional Medicare Tax above USD 200,000, the Net Investment Income Tax, employer-side tax, itemised deductions and the QBI deduction are not modelled.
Other states not researched; combined brackets are Austin, Texas (federal only).

rent_1bed_monthly.description: Unweighted mean of three popular central-Austin neighbourhood averages on RentCafe (Yardi Matrix), 1-bedroom: Downtown USD 2,841 (about 793 sq ft, 2026-09-30), Zilker USD 2,028 (755 sq ft, 2026-09-21), South Congress USD 1,367 (741 sq ft, 2026-09-30) = USD 2,079. Pages: https://www.rentcafe.com/average-rent-market-trends/us/tx/austin/downtown-austin/ , .../zilker/ , .../south-congress/. Citywide cross-checks: RentCafe USD 1,427 (2026-09-30); Zumper USD 1,305 (30-day average, 2026-10-15). Asking rents of apartment buildings, unfurnished.

rent_2bed_monthly.description: Unweighted mean of the same three RentCafe (Yardi Matrix) neighbourhood averages, 2-bedroom: Downtown USD 4,318 (about 1,269 sq ft), Zilker USD 2,664 (1,095 sq ft), South Congress USD 1,633 (1,063 sq ft) = USD 2,872. Citywide cross-checks: RentCafe USD 1,822 (2026-09-30); Zumper USD 1,650 (2026-10-15). Asking rents, unfurnished.

costs.notes: Asking rents, not median signed leases; Downtown is far dearer than South Congress, so the mean of three areas is an approximation, not a market median. Coworking not sourced: only unopened or undated search snippets were found. Cross-check source: Zumper https://www.zumper.com/rent-research/austin-tx (Austin citywide 1-bed USD 1,305, 2-bed USD 1,650, 2026-10-15).

residence_routes: There is no digital nomad visa. EU and many other nationals can visit on ESTA or B-1/B-2 status but may not work for US clients while there, so a remote worker has no direct immigration route; long stays need a work visa (H-1B, L-1, O-1, TN for Canada/Mexico), an investor visa or family sponsorship, all employer- or relationship-based. US citizens need no immigration route but owe US tax on worldwide income wherever they live. A skilled employee at a US employer typically uses H-1B (annual lottery), L-1 intra-company transfer or O-1.
open_questions: No nomad visa or special regime exists; covers_local_work does not apply.
